newsitem.title: USA: Chicago mayor unveils plan to renovate stadium.
newsitem.headline: Chicago mayor unveils plan to renovate stadium.

text.p: Mayor Richard Daley unveiled a plan on Friday to spend $395 million to renovate Chicago's aging professional football stadium, Soldier Field, and add a retractable roof.
The cost of the renovation plan would be covered by a $175 million fee from the sole tenant, the National Football League's Chicago Bears, and with bond sales to be paid off with entertainment taxes.

Bears' owner Michael McCaskey has been at odds with the mayor about whether to build a new domed stadium, which would cost in excess of $400 million. Daley has said he prefers an open-air stadium with a grass field, such as Soldier Field, and that convention space was adequate in the city so a new stadium was not needed.

The mayor's latest plan called for newly built two-tiered luxury skyboxes, a restaurant, a museum for the Bears, 2,000 additional seats, and a mechanized roof that could cover the grass field in 20 minutes.
It would also include a covered walkway to the nearby McCormick Place convention center, allowing Soldier Field to be used for other events.
